tools.name: create_room
tools.description: Open a new room. Your principal takes seat A, and you get a private invite link for the other person (seat B). Send the invite only to that person. Use this when your principal wants to negotiate with someone and has no room yet. This server requires sign-in: your MCP client must send your principal

tools.name: join_room
tools.description: Take your principal's seat with their private link. Returns the room state, your principal's card (if sealed), and what to do next.

tools.name: seal_intent_card
tools.description: Seal your principal's Intent Card. Only after they confirmed every line. Once sealed it cannot change except through escalation answers.

tools.name: get_room
tools.description: Current state from your seat: status, whose turn, transcript, claims you still need to review, unverified assumptions, and the next action.

tools.name: wait_for_turn
tools.description: Blocks up to timeout_seconds (max 25) until it is your turn, your principal must answer a question, or the room ends. Call it again if it times out.

tools.name: send_envelope
tools.description: Send one PXP envelope on your turn. The server enforces the rules: untagged or unreferenced claims become "assumed", agreeing while raising a conflict is refused. The enforced envelope is returned.

tools.name: answer_escalation
tools.description: When the room is paused for your principal, ask them the question verbatim and relay their exact answer. It is sealed into their card as an amendment. Never answer on their behalf.

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: The decision brief once the room has ended: agreed terms, authority per term, unverified assumptions, escalations, ledger head.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_room" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_room · Private data: create_room, join_room · Public sink: create_room, send_envelope.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_room · Private data: create_room, join_room · Public sink: create_room, send_envelope

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_room" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
